summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with severe COPD, chronic alcohol abuse, and chronic pain from prior trauma, was admitted after being found hypoxemic by EMTs near a transit station. He was transferred to the MICU for persistent hypoxemia and risk of alcohol withdrawal. His condition was attributed to a COPD exacerbation with atelectasis, worsened by poor medication adherence and recent alcohol intoxication. He was treated with steroids, antibiotics, duoneb treatments, and diazepam for CIWA scores indicating moderate withdrawal. His hypernatremia resolved with IV fluids. Despite clinical improvement, including being weaned off oxygen, he left against medical advice on the morning of April 22, aware of the risks. He declined discharge medications and follow-up planning.
